name: Playwright
summary: A browser automation and testing system that separates browser processes, isolated browser contexts, pages, protocol dispatch, and test-runner fixtures while exposing tracing and network control APIs.

features.name: Browser context isolation
features.description: The fixed server source models BrowserContext as a browser-owned object with its own pages, request context, options, and tracing state. Official documentation describes contexts as isolated, incognito-like environments that can be created independently within a browser.
benefits: Separates cookies, storage, pages, and permissions between test sessions
Allows multiple isolated sessions to share a browser process
costs: Context creation and browser resources add lifecycle overhead
Isolation does not remove host and browser process resource limits

features.name: Page and protocol object model
features.description: The fixed source defines Page as a server-side SDK object and routes browser-context page creation through the page object lifecycle. Playwright's protocol and dispatcher layers expose browser, context, page, network, and tracing operations across language clients.
benefits: Gives tests a stable page-level automation boundary
Centralizes browser-specific protocol handling behind common objects
costs: Protocol capabilities and browser differences remain observable
Asynchronous page lifecycle requires explicit waiting and cleanup

features.name: Fixture-scoped test composition
features.description: The official test-runner documentation defines fixtures as reusable setup and teardown resources with scopes and dependencies. Test projects compose these fixtures with browser and context creation to make isolation and shared setup explicit at the runner boundary.
benefits: Makes setup, teardown, and resource scope reusable
Supports project-specific browser configuration and parallel test organization
costs: Fixture dependency graphs can obscure setup order and ownership
Incorrect scope choices can leak state or increase startup cost

features.name: Context tracing boundary
features.description: BrowserContext owns a Tracing object in the fixed source, and the official tracing documentation exposes start, stop, and trace-viewer workflows for recording browser actions, snapshots, screenshots, and network information.
benefits: Associates diagnostic artifacts with an isolated test context
Provides post-failure inspection beyond assertion output
costs: Tracing consumes storage and may add runtime overhead
Trace capture must be coordinated with context lifecycle and sensitive data policy

mathematical_views.question: How do browser processes, contexts, pages, and request resources compose while preserving session boundaries?
assumptions: A browser contains one or more contexts
A context owns pages and context-scoped resources
Browser engine implementation details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which setup and teardown transitions are induced by fixture scopes and dependencies around a test?
assumptions: Fixtures are resources with setup and teardown phases
Runner scheduling and worker implementation are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which page, context, and network events can be projected into a replayable diagnostic artifact?
assumptions: A trace is a projection of context-scoped events
Trace capture has explicit start and stop boundaries
The model does not claim complete replay equivalence

benefits: Independent sessions can share a browser executable
costs: Isolation and context lifecycle consume resources

benefits: Common page objects hide protocol transport details
costs: Async lifecycle and browser-specific behavior remain test concerns

benefits: Reusable setup makes test resource ownership explicit
costs: Scope errors can cause leaks or unnecessary startup work
Capture overhead and artifact handling require policy
